item.content:encoded:
Home / Finance / News / RBI's 6-hour reporting rule could help curb cyber threats, frauds

RBI's 6-hour reporting rule could help curb cyber threats, frauds The directive requires all non-bank payment system operators (PSOs) to notify the central bank of such incidents in a prescribed format within the stipulated six-hour window

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) also mandates payment firms to report any cybersecurity incident to CERT-In within six hours of fraud detection (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 15 2026 | 3:24 PM IST

Listen to This Article

The RBI's recent comprehensive master guidelines mandating non-bank payment system operators to report unusual incidents, including cyberattacks, critical system outages, and settlement delays, within six hours of detection are aimed at strengthening cybersecurity and curbing the growing menace of digital fraud, experts said. The directive requires all non-bank payment system operators (PSOs) to notify the central bank of such incidents in a prescribed format within the stipulated six-hour window, enabling quicker regulatory intervention and better monitoring of potential threats to the payments ecosystem. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) also mandates payment firms to report any cybersecurity incident to CERT-In within six hours of fraud detection.

Experts said the move assumes significance amid the rapid expansion of digital transactions and the growing sophistication of cyber threats targeting payment infrastructure. The RBI's revised Master Directions on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank Payment System Operators apply to the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), card networks, payment aggregators, prepaid payment instrument (PPI) issuers, and white-label ATM operators (WLAOs), among others. Also Read

The central bank has introduced rigorous requirements for digital transactions, software security, system audits, and third-party service providers to prescribe new cyber safeguards for PSOs. Welcoming the RBI's revised and stricter cybersecurity guidelines, 63SATS Cybertech Joint MD and CEO Srinivas L said, "The RBI has turned scattered circulars into one clear rulebook, and that removes all excuses. The most significant is the requirement to hold the source code of critical third-party applications or keep it in escrow".

"Many payment breaches today do not begin inside the company. They begin in vendor software that nobody inside fully understands. You cannot defend what you cannot see. Together with annual system audits, tight incident reporting, and mobile device binding, this moves cybersecurity from the IT room to the boardroom, where it belongs," he said. The RBI requires every PSO to submit an annual system audit report within two months of the end of its financial year. It retains the mandatory 12-hour cooling-off period after a customer changes their registered mobile number or email address. According to Apollo Infoways founder and CEO Ravi Prakash, "The mandatory six-hour cyber incident reporting window sends a clear message that cybersecurity can no longer remain a reactive compliance function. The RBI has taken a strategic step towards making India's digital payment ecosystem more intelligent".

The revised cybersecurity framework issued earlier this month marks a significant milestone in shaping India's next generation of secure and resilient digital financial infrastructure, he added. The new rules are already in effect for large and medium PSOs. However, small PSOs have been given time until April 1, 2028, to comply. "This regulation underscores the shift from reactive security to proactive cyber resilience. The six-hour reporting window will compel payment operators to invest in stronger monitoring, incident response, and risk management frameworks," Nerix Technoserve CEO Subhasis Majumdar said. The RBI has also prescribed stricter business continuity arrangements. The operators must maintain disaster recovery facilities in a different seismic zone from their primary data centres and conduct recovery drills at least twice a year.

Srinivas pointed out, "India runs one of the world's largest digital payment systems, and every operator in that chain must be as strong as the bank at its end. Compliance is the floor, while resilience is the goal".

item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / What travellers need to know about US flights after nationwide ground stop

What travellers need to know about US flights after nationwide ground stop The longest flight stoppage in 25 years lasted more than four hours and ended around 8:15 pm ET Friday, allowing some domestic flights to take off from US airports

Travelers sit on a baggage carousel during a nationwide ground stop at LaGuardia Airport (LGA) in the Queens borough of New York, US, on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. A nationwide ground stop was canceled by the Federal Aviation Administr | Image: Bloomberg

AP Washington 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 15 2026 | 11:15 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Officials assured passengers that the US airspace was safe and operational after a nationwide ground stop that was initiated out of caution caused massive travel disruptions. The longest flight stoppage in 25 years lasted more than four hours and ended around 8:15 pm ET Friday, allowing some domestic flights to take off from US airports. Of the 41,000 flights scheduled Saturday, more than 6,400 had been canceled by Saturday night, according to FlightAware. More than 800 flights scheduled for Sunday were cancelled, it said. But officials said the air traffic control system was operational and expected airline schedules to fully recover by the end of Sunday, smoothing out ahead of the Thanksgiving travel rush.

Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication the failure was related to a cyberattack and no lives were at risk. Also Read

US air travel woes to persist into Sunday as thousands of flights hit

US air travel should recover from ground stop by end of Sunday, FAA says

US transportation secy seeks $50 bn emergency air traffic upgrade funds

US authorities lift nationwide flight ground stop after 4-hour disruption

Flights halted at airports across US due to ATC communications problems

Here's what to know: Flights have resumed but disruption continues Federal Aviation Administration Administrator Bryan Bedford said the system was stable Saturday. Several thousand flights were able to fly after the ground stop, but ultimately, some 12,000 scheduled flights were unable to take off Friday, he said. Officials acknowledged the disruption but said safety was paramount. Bedford offered an apology for stranded travelers and thanked air traffic controllers, pilots and flight attendants for managing the fallout. He said officials were confident the system is operating safely or else they would keep airplanes on the ground.

Airlines remove change fees for affected passengers Airlines are obligated to offer free rebooking on another flight or a full refund if a flight is cancelled. Bedford said the administration was working closely with airlines and said they were waiving all terms and conditions. Some airlines were allowing passengers to rebook if they had travel scheduled Friday or Saturday. Others extended the offer to people with reservations for Sunday or even Monday. Bedford advised passengers to contact their airlines. The system was overloaded while part of it was being upgraded A contractor was replacing a section of the system's old and discontinued copper wire with new fiber wire in a remote location Friday afternoon, Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said Saturday. That kind of work has been happening across the country and across industries for decades, he said.

But on Friday, the router in that location started overloading the air traffic control system and causing intermittent disruptions to communications and radar feeds. When officials couldn't quickly locate the cause of the overload, they grounded flights nationwide. "We did that out of an abundance of caution," Bedford said. "I'm sorry that we put you through this, but we did it for the right reasons."   Officials stressed that the ground stop was not the result of a system outage or nefarious activity by a foreign actor. Duffy said officials were investigating whether contractor error or a faulty router was the cause. The air traffic control modernization began last year after Congress approved USD 12.5 billion of funding. Duffy and the White House are pushing for $30 billion more to complete the work. About 70 per cent of copper wire has been switched to fiber already, officials said Saturday.

The Microsoft outage was unrelated to the stoppage Microsoft said Saturday that services were fully restored after its own massive outage. There was no indication the FAA ground stop was related to the service disruption that took Microsoft services offline Thursday, according to federal officials and a company spokesperson. Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft said on its website. Users reported Microsoft 365 services including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot were interrupted.
